source.title: Steering Safely or Off a Cliff? Rethinking Specificity and Robustness in Inference-Time Interventions

page_placements.theme: Over-refusal along the refusal direction and its targeted repair

record.tranche_reason: The study uses difference-in-means and other steering directions, including a direction-ablation method, as interventions for reducing overrefusal. It evaluates the performance and safety effects of those interventions, but does not test the claim’s harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction with the claimed all-layer, all-position ablation or addition.
record.gate_note: Rows cover Table 2’s explicit-control overrefusal results for canonical harmful-query safety, jailbreak robustness, and MMLU. These are outcomes of the study’s own steering interventions, not tests of the specific refusal direction in the claim, so they are recorded as none. Hyperparameter choices, cited results from other work, and the plotted activation geometry are not rows. Table 2’s GSM8K and fluency results, Table 5’s without-explicit-control results, and Table 4’s hallucination-steering results are left out; see rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: The study learns overrefusal-reduction vectors (DiffMean on compliant vs refusal demonstrations, probes, SSV, ReFT-r1, PartialOR) and adds or ablates them at one layer and position. It reports only its own steering's efficacy and specificity. It never ablates or adds the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction to test whether that direction mediates refusal. PartialOR computes a true-refusal direction, but only to orthogonalize the false-refusal vector. Its effect alone is not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the same pattern appears in faithfulness-hallucination steering, where robustness to distractor context drops. Add that results without explicit control (Table 5) match the controlled ones.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses difference-in-means and related vector-learning methods, but learns overrefusal-reduction vectors and intervenes at a selected layer and token position. PartialOR ablates a false-refusal direction; this is not the claimed harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction ablated at every layer and position. Repo and code are available, but the paper says it will not release specific intervention parameters.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect varies by steering method and model. The study reports different trade-offs across methods; explicit-control and without-explicit-control settings show similar overall trends. Interventions are selected from a search over layers, the last 5 token positions, and steering factors.

fits_no_version.finding: Overrefusal steering, even with explicit harmful-refusal control, keeps canonical harmful-query safety mostly intact. Safety under jailbreak prefixes drops across all 4 models and 5 methods (e.g., Llama-8B −0.19 to −0.30). MMLU is mostly unchanged except SSV on Qwen-7B (−0.29).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering to reduce overrefusal preserves in-distribution refusal of harmful queries but increases jailbreak susceptibility.

fits_no_version.finding: In the top-2 principal components at layer 20, last token, activations of jailbreak-prefixed harmful queries lie close to harmless queries in all four models (Fig. 4, Fig. 5). This is a PCA projection, not a projection onto a refusal direction, and no intervention tests it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak prefixes shift harmful-query activations toward the harmless cluster in early-PC space.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The experiments cover four instruction-tuned models up to 8B parameters and a single-task setup. The paper reports significance testing at p<0.05 and averages over 3 runs, but the extracted table does not provide row-specific uncertainty values. The authors also note that evaluations are on generated text and that larger models are outside the study’s compute scope.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 GSM8K and fluency rows were omitted to stay within 60 rows after retaining canonical safety, jailbreak robustness, and MMLU results. Table 5 (without explicit control), Table 4 (faithfulness hallucination steering), and the activation PCA figures were omitted because the retained Table 2 results were prioritized for the claim’s refusal and capability-related outcomes.

untested.parts: Not tested: ablating or adding the harmful-minus-harmless direction, and its effect on refusal and capabilities. The study's DiffMean is computed over compliant vs refusal demonstrations for pseudo-harmful queries, not harmful vs harmless instructions.
No weight edit or abliterated released model.
Not tested: whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction, or training against its ablation. Jailbreak success is measured only after overrefusal steering.
Not tested: whether refusal is one direction or several.
Not tested: harmfulness encoded separately from refusal. The true/false-refusal split serves only to build PartialOR's vector.
No transfer across languages or model variants.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T4 / uses_without_test call and all-none row links are right. Row values match Table 2. Relative drops in the text (e.g., 47% MMLU for SSV on Qwen-7B, 35–55% robustness drop for Llama-8B) are relative to baseline, not absolute deltas. Table 2 bolding for significance cannot be read in the extracted text, so the absent/partial states rest on the authors' prose.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the claimed harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, all-layer/all-position ablation, addition-induced harmless refusals, or the full capability-preservation claim using that direction.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Jailbreak vulnerability is measured after overrefusal steering, but the study does not test whether attacks suppress the claimed direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
The study does not test whether refusal is better represented as an affine set, cone, or dominant direction plus others.
No separate harmfulness-judgment versus refusal-decision representation is tested.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer of the claimed direction is tested.
The study compares steering with and without explicit control examples, but does not test whether refusal training determines whether a single removable direction exists.

relation.reason: Uses difference-in-means style steering (citing Arditi et al. for DiffMean and for steering at a single layer and position) as a tool for overrefusal reduction. No result tests any claim version.

tranche.reason: Learns overrefusal-reduction vectors from compliant vs refusal demonstrations, or a false-refusal vector orthogonalized against harmful-minus-harmless (PartialOR), and reports only its own steering's efficacy and specificity. It never ablates or adds the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction alone and measures refusal.

source_check.notes: The bold and underline significance marks in Table 2 are lost in the text. Per Section 7, only LinearProbe on Llama-8B (-10%) and DiffMean, LinearProbe and ReFT-r1 on Llama-3B (7-8%) are notable canonical-safety drops. The record's verdict 'none' is right. Figure 4/5 PCA (last token, layer 20) shows jailbreak-prefixed harmful activations near harmless ones. That fits V3, but it is figure-only and measures no refusal direction. The authors_conclusion additions check out: B.1 hallucination robustness drops, and B.2/Table 5 match the controlled setting.

statements.problem: Correct. Table 2 (explicit control), Llama-8B +Jailbreak column: -0.28, -0.30, -0.19, -0.23, -0.25, so the range is -0.19 to -0.30. All 20 jailbreak cells across 4 models and 5 methods are negative. Minor: the cited rows R01/R02 are canonical-query rows, not the jailbreak cells the numbers come from. The text gives the same drop as 35-55% relative to a 0.55 baseline.
